Allow ADB from afar via Tailscale

Makes ADB reachable inside your tailnet, not on the public internet. Any tailnet device with an approved ADB key gets full shell access to this car screen. ADB already accepts connections from your local network, and switching this off does not change that.
Remote ADB is on in your tailnet

While this is on, MQTT to public brokers (HiveMQ, AWS IoT and the like) will not work, because Tailscale only reaches your tailnet. Saving restarts the service.
Choose the option that fits your car screen. Default suits older panoramic cameras. DiLink 4 uses the AVM SurfaceTexture path. DiLink 5 uses the SA8155P qcarcam_test bridge.
Default — fits Seal, Atto, Dolphin (most cars)
Switching the mode restarts the camera service. If the picture looks wrong (squashed, missing corners, red overlay), try the other mode.
The camera IDs are listed as front, right, rear, left. Leave it on Auto, unless the raw previews clearly show a different order for this car.
Front and rear, left and right swapped — 2,3,0,1

This camera order is already chosen.
Per-car adjustments for the DiLink 4 path. They only work when DiLink 4 is selected above.
Switch on only what your car needs. Restarting the camera service applies the change.

Leaves the car\'s own panorama output alone and records preview port 0 as it comes. Use this if forced panorama control opens the red calibration screen. Some models then show two views instead of four.

Adds a shader step that spots the bright-red pixels of the HAL message \"calibration failed\" and swaps them for a neighbouring pixel (or grey, if the banner is too big to repair). Looks only: the real calibration state stays as it is.
Choose where the panoramic picture comes from
Auto picks the right camera for your model at every start. Camera 1 = BYD Seal, camera 0 = Atto. After you change the camera ID, restart the service so it takes effect.
ID of the car\'s own drive camera

Choose the AVMCamera ID that points to the front drive-camera sensor. It is the opposite of the panorama: Seal/Han panorama = 1 → drive camera = 0; Atto / Tang panorama = 0 → drive camera = 1. Leave on Auto and Panoptes picks.
Auto — panorama ID is %1$d, so the drive camera can\'t be worked out
Test two cameras at once on the next start

A one-off check that opens both cameras together, to see whether this car can run panorama and drive camera side by side. It runs once at the next restart while parked. Keep it OFF unless clips look wrong. It isn\'t needed and can briefly interrupt a running recording.

Copies each camera frame before encoding, so a stuck recording can never starve the car\'s own reverse-camera picture. Only for the older camera mode. Uses about 60 MB of GPU memory and one extra GPU pass per frame. Applies after the next camera restart (ignition cycle or service restart).
The previews follow your ID choices. If the two pictures look mixed up, tap Switch. It swaps both IDs and saves right away. Need a specific ID? Open the manual camera IDs below.
Switch the 360° and drive camera IDs
Set camera IDs by hand — advanced
These tiles show which camera feeds the 360° view and which one is the front drive camera. If the two pictures look swapped, tap Switch to swap and save both IDs. Then carry on.
The camera the 360° pipeline opens. It feeds the 2×2 mosaic used for recording (cam_*.mp4), Guardian and live cameras. The pairing card above shows the same choice.
The camera the car\'s own drive-camera recorder opens for dvr_*.mp4 clips. It is separate from the windshield role below, which only changes the top strip of the drive-camera layout.
Slice setup: chooses which part of the 360° mosaic shows this direction. It does not change which camera is opened.
Windshield role: the picture used as the top strip of the drive-camera layout and for windshield streaming. Independent of the front drive camera ID above.
Cabin role: an optional interior picture for layouts and streaming.
No preview yet. Try another candidate, or reopen this dialog once the service has restarted.

By default Panoptes starts the way it always did. Here you can set up the joined panorama strip properly. Look at each raw slice, assign the 360° roles to the slice that really shows front, right, rear and left on your car, and after a restart the service uses that layout for recording, streaming and AI.
Three short steps and you\'re set:
Starts with the language of your car screen. Tap to pick another one for the Panoptes app and the web page.
Tap below to open BYD Auto-Start. Find Panoptes in the list and untick it. BYD resets this with every install, so you\'ll need to repeat it after updates.
Autostart couldn\'t be turned on by itself. BYD Auto-Start is opening so you can do it by hand.
BYD reset the autostart permission with the install. Without it the app stops in the background.
“Display over other apps” is not allowed yet. Without it, the Panoptes display on screen is missing.
Show on top of other apps
Switch this on to see a small floating status for recording and the logbook above other apps.
Panoptes reads your cameras through a small helper on this device. Android asks once to allow USB debugging. Tap Allow and tick Always allow from this device, so it keeps working after every restart.
Accept the Android pop-up. Can\'t see it? Maybe it was already allowed, and this goes on by itself.
The helper isn\'t running yet. Maybe the Android pop-up was closed. Try again and remember to tick Always allow.

Choose what Panoptes does after you switch the car off.

Always on keeps watching while parked. Guardian and background checks stay active, so the car uses a little power overnight.

Drive only shuts Panoptes down completely when you leave. Drive camera, logbook and charging still work while you drive, and everything starts again by itself when you switch the car on. You can change this any time in Settings.

Panoptes can check GitHub every 6 hours for a new version. GitHub then sees the car\'s IP address and the time; nothing else is sent. Nothing is installed without you: you decide in Settings whether updates are only shown or installed automatically while parked.\n\nYou can change this any time under System → App updates.

A live preview is loading from your cameras. A few seconds, please.
Use the arrows to find the joined picture with four views. Read it from the BOTTOM: bottom left is the REAR, bottom right is the LEFT side.
Next, find the camera that looks ahead
Click through the cameras with the arrows and stop at the one that shows the windshield or the road ahead. Remember its number, you\'ll pick it next.
In the top card, choose the number of your 360° or normal camera. Unsure? Leave it on AUTO and Panoptes works it out.
In this card, choose the drive camera number you found before, or leave it on AUTO.
The picture goes dark and flickers for about 10 seconds. That\'s normal, just wait.
Does the 360° view show the joined picture, and does the drive camera show the road ahead? If a picture looks wrong, tap Choose again. Nothing is broken.
For the car\'s own drive-camera layout, with the windshield camera as a strip above your recording: pick Windshield in the role menu, choose the front camera and save. Most owners can skip this.
Choose your model and the kWh fill in by themselves, or type them yourself (5–120). This makes range and charging estimates accurate. You can skip it and set it later.
These cards are buttons. Tap them to open Live cameras, Clips, Services or your car.
The chips at the top show recording, services and your remote access. They refresh by themselves and aren\'t buttons.
Your live status for recording, services and remote access is shown here. It refreshes by itself.
Cameras assigned and battery saved. Tap Live cameras to see your pictures, or look through the deeper settings whenever you like.
Setup reset — the guide plays again
A short walk through the deeper settings: your car profile, connections, Guardian, diagnostics, services and security. Stop whenever you like.
Tap the car tile to enter your battery size and model. It makes range and battery health estimates accurate.
Switch between Drive camera (continuous and close-by clips) and Guardian (clips from when parked) with this toggle. Each keeps its own library. Tap a clip to play it.
Open Live cameras here to see all cameras as they happen. Handy for checking the view before you drive off, or while you\'re parked nearby.
The logbook records every drive: route, distance, time and energy use. So you can look back at where the car has been.

Road watch uses the car\'s motion sensors and GPS to spot road hazards such as bumps and potholes, and warns you before known ones. Its tabs cover detection, the hazard map, warning sounds and the blind spot view. Turn on the main switch to use any of it.

Switch on the blind spot view in the tab here. When you signal a turn, a side camera picture pops up by itself, left for left and right for right, and goes away shortly after. It only runs while a turn signal is on.

Open the map for full turn-by-turn navigation: search a destination, get the route and live guidance, plus places nearby and any road hazards Road watch has logged along the way. You can also show it on the instrument cluster when you start driving. That switch is in the Map tab of Road watch.
Link Telegram alerts, the route planner link (ABRP), a smart home link (MQTT) or your BYD account. Each card opens its setup inside the app. The pill at the top turns green when everything is linked.
Your BYD account unlocks remote control
Linking your BYD account here lets you lock, flash and honk from your phone. Treat the linked account and the access code as private.
Tune detection, quality and storage here. These open as pages in the app, served from your car. A blank screen only means the helper is still starting.
This reassigns which physical camera serves each role and restarts the cameras. Change it only if a picture looks wrong. You set this up earlier in the guide.
Traffic monitor — needed for remote access
BYD\'s built-in traffic monitor stops other apps from using the car\'s own SIM. To reach your car remotely over the BYD SIM, switch it off here. The car screen reboots to apply the change.
These switches start and stop background services. If you switch Camera, Guardian or Guardian on park OFF, recording stops and stays off until you switch it back on, even after a restart.
Set a PIN to lock the app when others use the car. Guardian and recording keep running while the app is locked. A forgotten PIN can only be cleared from a computer over USB.
This erases clips, events and settings and cannot be undone. It\'s here for the day you sell the car, not for everyday use.
You\'ve now seen the deeper settings. Start this guide again any time with the help button.

The BYD Traffic Monitor (com.byd.trafficmonitor) is a built-in app that keeps checking road traffic in the background.

Why turn it off?

• It uses mobile data, even when parked
• It uses processor power and battery in the background
• You do not need it if you use another navigation app
• It can get in the way of the Drive camera’s network use

It is safe to turn off. It only removes the traffic colours on the built-in map. Navigation, Bluetooth and everything else in the car keep working.

Afterwards you need a hard reboot (hold the centre console button for 5 seconds).

This lets devices on your tailnet reach ADB (port 5555), so you can debug this car screen from afar.

Before you turn it on:
• ADB gives FULL control: a tailnet device with an approved key can read data, install apps and change system settings
• Only your tailnet gets this new route. ADB is not opened to the public internet
• ADB already accepts connections from your local network, so turning this off does not close ADB completely
• The connecting computer still needs an approved ADB key
• Turning on the Wi-Fi hotspot drops the Wi-Fi link, so remote access then relies on mobile data

Only turn this on for a tailnet you control. You can turn it off any time.

MQTT will then travel through Tailscale, so you can reach a private broker in your tailnet without port forwarding.

While it is on:
• MQTT to a broker in your tailnet works (for example Mosquitto on a device in your tailnet)
• MQTT to public brokers (HiveMQ, AWS IoT and so on) will fail, because Tailscale only reaches your tailnet
• The Tailscale service restarts to apply the change
• Other app traffic and the rest of the device are not affected

You can turn it off any time.

This will:
• Stop Tailscale if it is running
• Remove the Tailscale setup from this device
• You still need to remove the device in the Tailscale console

Opens the proxy to devices on the hotspot. Each device must be set to use it. Just joining the hotspot is not enough.

Joining the hotspot alone gets a device nowhere. This car can't pass internet on by itself, so every device has to be told to use the car's proxy.

On the device, after it has joined:
1. Open its WLAN settings and edit this network
2. Set Proxy to Manual
3. Host name %1$s, port %2$d
4. Save and start browsing

The device may still say "no internet" and show its own mobile data icon while all is fine, because that check ignores proxies. Apps that skip the WLAN proxy (some streaming and games) won't work.

The car has only one WLAN chip. It can\'t run a hotspot and sit in another WLAN at once. While the hotspot is on, the car leaves your WLAN and uses its SIM card data, for itself and for every connected device. Your WLAN returns when you switch the hotspot off.
